Here, we use the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the ${cos}^{2}⁡x$ term, given by

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2x=2{cos}^{2}⁡x-1.
$$

 

Rearranging, we have

$$
2{cos}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+1.
$$

Substituting this into the expression $4{cos}^{2}⁡x-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2x,$ we get

$$
4{cos}^{2}⁡x-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2x=2(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+1)-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2x=2.
$$

Thus, the integral becomes

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}(4{cos}^{2}⁡x-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}2\,\text{d}x \\  & =2x{|}_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4} \\  & =2(\frac{\pi }{4}-(-\frac{\pi }{4})) \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
